pricing_negotiation_summary: Current ask: Dedicated reserved capacity for core support-agent workload + burst during campaigns. Draft commercial terms discussed: committed baseline = 2M tokens/month (guaranteed reserved capacity) at $0.06 per 1k tokens effective; burst allowance = up to 40% above commit for short windows (30-min sliding) with pre-authorized burst budget. Overage pricing tiers: tier1 (up to 120% of commit) at 1.15x committed unit price, tier2 (120-160%) at 1.5x, spot/ondemand beyond 160% at 2.0x. Ramp schedule proposal: month1-3: billing at 50% of committed (ramp credit applied), month4-6: 75%, month7: full committed billing. Optional auto-burst carveouts for marketing events (one-off agreed credits). Proposed minimum term 12 months with quarterly usage reviews and headroom adjustment. They requested clearer language on how continuous batching and KV-caching affect token billing; provided whitepaper link. Negotiation points outstanding: commit size (2M vs 3M tokens), burst percent (40% vs requested 60%), overage caps, and whether burst minutes roll into next billing cycle. Procurement also pushing for SLA credits tied to latency for chat route.
requirements_summary: Latency p50 target 150-250ms for chat; throughput target 70 requests/min sustained for peak route; embeddings <50ms avg; VPC peering + private endpoints; per-route cost breakdown; SOC2 + audit logs; EU residency for PII records. Prefers model family: opensource-based curated (they want Redwood-verified performance), fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost control.
